name: Shakers (United Society of Believers)

facts.value: Manchester group under the Wardleys in the 18th century. Ann Lee joined 1758, came to America 1774. First society at New Lebanon 1787

citations.excerpt: Mother Ann arrived on the 6th of August 1774 in New York City.
organized in 1787 (before any formal organization in Watervliet) the New Lebanon Society, the first Shaker Society

disagreements.excerpt: The United Society of Believers was founded in 1747.

citations.excerpt: was applied in the early 18th century to a Manchester offshoot of the English Quakers, who, led by James and Ann Wardley, accepted the peculiar doctrines of the French Prophets

facts.value: Ann Lee, after James and Ann Wardley

citations.excerpt: The Wardleys were succeeded by the real founder of Shakerism, Ann Lee (1736–1784)

facts.value: Celibate and communal, pacifist, with trembling, jumping and dancing in worship.

citations.excerpt: SHAKERS, an American celibate and communistic sect
The group is pacifistic and celibate; the only remaining Shakers live in the Sabbathday Lake Village in Maine.
writhed and trembled so that they won the name Shakers; their trances and visions, their jumping and dancing, were like those of many other sects

facts.value_before_verify: Celibate and communal, pacifist, with ecstatic dance in worship.

research_notes: Outside lane. EB1911 names the Wardleys James and Ann Wardley.
